chunks: And Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who hired a laborer, and neither of them trusted the other, so the wage was placed in the hands of a man. Then that man died, leaving no means of repayment, and the wage was lost.

He said: The employer is liable for the wage of the laborer until he pays it, unless the laborer was the one who called him to that and was satisfied with it. If he did that, then his right is where he placed it and with what he was satisfied.

key_terms.الْأَجْرَ: the wage or payment due for labor
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable or responsible to compensate
key_terms.فَرَضِيَ بِهِ: he consented to it and accepted the arrangement

ai.seo_question: Who is responsible if a worker’s wage deposited with a third party is lost?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about liability for wages when payment is entrusted to a third party. The employer remains responsible for the laborer’s wage if the entrusted intermediary dies and the money is lost, unless the laborer himself requested that arrangement and accepted it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3658 - Harun bin Hamzah Al-Ghanawi narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

I asked him about a man who hired a laborer, but neither of them trusted the other, so they deposited the wages with a third person. Then that third person died without leaving anything to cover the wages, and the wages were lost.

Imam (as) said: 'The employer is responsible for the wages of the laborer until they are settled, unless the laborer had invited the employer to do so and agreed to it. If he did, then his right is where he placed it and what he agreed upon.'
